newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends down despite run to new high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends down despite run to new high.

text.p: CSCE world sugar ended lower after hitting new life-of-contract highs in October in roller-coaster trading instigated by the trade and dominated by funds.
The trade began the selling early, one commission house broker said, triggering fund buy-stops "all the way up," particularly at 11.70 cents and again at 11.80 cents a pound.

"And then all of a sudden the buying just stopped," the broker said. "There's no good reason for it. But as soon as the market paused, you had a round of selling, most likely older longs sensing a selling opportunity."
The October contract reached a high of 11.87 cents a lb before retreating to 11.59 cents a lb, down 0.09 cents from Wednesday's close, only 0.03 cents above the intra-day lows.
The result is a technical reversal that has some brokers looking for another sell-off Friday. "If the funds need a reason to sell, they have one now," one source said. "They've been long for weeks."

Fundamentally, the market looks strong, said Corey Bell, an analyst with Dean Witter. "Based on the fundamentals, I would expect the market to test new highs," he said. "El Nino will likely be affecting crops this year and next. The India crop is off significantly, as is Thailand."
He added, however, that the sizable speculative long position would look to liquidate beneath support at 11.50 cents in th October contract.
((Derek J. Caney, New York Commodity Desk, 212-859-1646))
